hook_text: One rule makes any shape on the grid bigger or smaller without changing its shape.
clip_script: A triangle sits on the grid with corners 1 semicolon 1, 3 semicolon 1 and 1 semicolon 2. To enlarge it about the origin with scale factor 2, multiply both numbers of every corner by 2: 2 semicolon 2, 6 semicolon 2, 2 semicolon 4. Same shape, twice the size. Scale factor 3: multiply by 3. To shrink, use a scale factor smaller than 1: halve 4 semicolon 6 and you get 2 semicolon 3. Why does it work? Draw a ray from the origin through each corner. Every corner slides along its own ray until it is k times as far away. And here is the test: divide new by old. 2 semicolon 3 to 4 semicolon 9 gives 2 and 3, two different multipliers, so it is not an enlargement. Multiply both numbers, by the same k.
visual_style: A yellow triangle on a grid; rays fan out from the origin; blue and green copies appear twice and three times as far along the rays; a stretched fake gets a red cross.
pacing: Steady, one multiplication per beat, a pause on the rays.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for reductions, the area of the image and the five common errors.
